worldcombat.skill.switcheroo.summary: Slip past at a speed the eye cannot follow and swap held items on contact. Almost no wind-up and a short cooldown, at the cost of having to close in. Faster individuals slip further and trade more cleanly.
worldcombat.skill.switcheroo.use.0: Close in and take the foe's item
worldcombat.skill.switcheroo.use.1: Hand a burden to the foe in a close scuffle
worldcombat.skill.switcheroo.use.2: Swap through the foe and come out behind it
worldcombat.skill.switcheroo.description: Move up to %1$s blocks along your aim and swap held items on contact.
A %1$s wind-up and %2$s blocks per tick, then %3$s to gather yourself after the trade and a %4$s cooldown from commit.
Passing through carries you %1$s blocks past the target and drags it about %2$s blocks along the slip.
worldcombat.skill.switcheroo.through.on: Pass through: after the swap you keep going into the space behind the target (distance above), at the cost of ending up deep in their line.
worldcombat.skill.switcheroo.through.off: Stop on contact: after the swap you settle at the target's side, a steadier landing that never leaves its reach.
worldcombat.skill.switcheroo.timing: Cast within %1$s blocks; after %2$s seconds of preparation it costs %4$s PP to slip out, then %3$s seconds to gather yourself and a %5$s second cooldown from commit.
worldcombat.skill.switcheroo.growth.0: At level %1$s the slip reaches %2$s blocks and the cooldown becomes %3$s seconds.
worldcombat.skill.switcheroo.growth.1: At level %1$s the slip reaches %2$s blocks at %3$s blocks per tick, and the sparks rise to %4$s.
On: after the swap you keep going into the space behind the target (distance in Pass-through distance). Off: you stop on contact at the target's side, a steadier landing that never leaves its reach.
Only slip in within this distance; farther targets are left to the shared approach logic.
On: it will leave its station under a hold order to slip in. Off: it only slips when the target is already in reach.
Only when there is an item to trade
On: only used when the target or the caster holds an item. Off: it also slips past when both are empty-handed (usually for nothing).
